title: private-deploy-networking-incident-notes
content:
SUMMARY:
- Notes / breadcrumbs for private deployment networking incident affecting onboarding of pd-nyc cluster (customer: Acme Corp).
- Symptoms: control-plane (internal hostname control-plane.redwood.local) sometimes unreachable from customer VPC; intermittent TLS handshake failures; some outbound egress flows failing (S3 uploads timing out).
- Start: 2026-01-30 09:15 PST when onboarding tests failed.

ACTIONS/COMMANDS TRIED (raw outputs included where useful)
1) Verify basic reachability from customer bastion to control-plane IP (10.32.5.12)
- command: ssh ec2-user@bastion.acme -i ~/keys/acme.pem
- from bastion:
  $ ping -c 3 10.32.5.12
  PING 10.32.5.12 (10.32.5.12) 56(84) bytes of data.
  64 bytes from 10.32.5.12: icmp_seq=1 ttl=63 time=12.3 ms
  64 bytes from 10.32.5.12: icmp_seq=2 ttl=63 time=12.4 ms
  64 bytes from 10.32.5.12: icmp_seq=3 ttl=63 time=12.6 ms
  --- 10.32.5.12 ping statistics ---
  3 packets transmitted, 3 received, 0% packet loss, time 2002ms
=> ICMP OK from bastion to control-plane.

2) Check application TCP reachability and TLS handshake
- command: openssl s_client -connect control-plane.redwood.local:443 -servername control-plane.redwood.local -ign_eof -brief
- output (intermittent):
  CONNECTED(00000003)
  140735243454720:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1543:SSL alert number 48
  ---
  no peer certificate available
  ---
  
  SIGNALED: TLS handshake aborted by server (unknown CA) on some attempts; other attempts succeed with full cert chain.
=> Flaky TLS: suggests either different backend serving different certs OR intermittent MITM (unlikely) OR client hitting different network path that resolves to different instance.

3) DNS resolution from bastion + from control-plane subnet
- from bastion:
  $ dig +short @10.0.0.2 control-plane.redwood.local
  10.32.5.12
- from customer app host in overlay subnet (10.20.10.33) when failing:
  $ dig +short control-plane.redwood.local
  ; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
=> When failing, DNS queries time out for some hosts. Suggests conditional forwarding to Redwood private zone sometimes not reachable (VPC peering / routes to resolver broken).

4) Check VPC Peering status and route tables (AWS console + CLI)
- aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=redwood-acme-peer
  -> Peering connection pcx-0a1b2c3d "active" on both sides.
- describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-012345
  -> Route entry present for 10.32.0.0/16 -> pcx-0a1b2c3d in private subnets.
- BUT: route propagation for transit-gateway attachments missing on some subnets (we have mixed TGW + peering config).
=> Hypothesis: partial route overlap between TGW and peering causes asymmetric routing; some subnets send DNS to outbound resolver over TGW where security groups or NACLs block it.

5) Check security groups / NACLs for DNS/TLS ports
- confirmed SG on control-plane allows 443 from customer CIDR and SG on bastion allows 53/UDP outbound to resolver 10.0.0.2.
- NACLs on public subnets had default deny for ephemeral range egress on one of the AZs (bad config left during last change). Found rule denying UDP 1024-65535 egress -> breaks DNS responses when source port ephemeral used.
=> Fixed by allowing ephemeral ports in NACL for the affected subnet. Patch applied 2026-01-31 02:15 UTC. Note: still see flakiness after this change.

6) Egress/NAT checks (S3 uploads timing out)
- from control-plane host:
  $ curl -v https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-artifacts/test.txt
  * Connected to s3.amazonaws.com (52.218.32.12) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS handshake: SSL_connect error: certificate verify failed
  * Closing connection 0
  curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
- from app host in customer VPC: same error intermittently.
=> Investigated NAT gateway logs: scaling recently changed to NAT instance in one AZ; that instance missing updated CA bundle (we install system CA updates via SSM) -> certificate verification fails when hitting that NAT instance. Replacement NAT instance fixed CA issue for that AZ 2026-02-02 18:30 UTC.

7) Check for split-horizon DNS / resolver configuration mismatch
- customer uses their own resolver at 10.0.0.2 that forwards cc: redwood.local -> resolver.redwood.internal (10.32.5.2) via conditional forwarder across peering. When route asymmetry, forwarder traffic goes over TGW path which is blocked.
- Found inconsistent resolver config: route to 10.32.5.2 went via TGW in AZ-a, via peering in AZ-b. When hosts in AZ-a attempt to resolve, queries timed out.

8) Check TLS certs on control-plane instances for SAN and issuer
- command: ssh to control-plane-1; sudo cat /etc/ssl/certs/control-plane.crt | openssl x509 -noout -text
  Subject: CN=control-plane.redwood.local
  X509v3 Subject Alternative Name: DNS:control-plane.redwood.local, DNS:internal.control.redwood.local
  Issuer: CN=Redwood Internal CA
- Problem: some client paths expect a public CA chain (because they go through an egress NAT which intercepts and re-signs certs for monitoring), resulting in unknown CA errors. We saw both unknown CA and successful handshakes.
=> Hypothesis: traffic path determines whether intermediate CA is trusted. Confirmed by comparing trust stores on NAT instance mentioned above.

TIMELINE (concise)
- 2026-01-30 09:15 PST: onboarding tests fail.
- 2026-01-30 10:00 PST: Initial triage shows ICMP OK but intermittent DNS/TLS.
- 2026-01-31 02:15 UTC: NACL ephemeral egress rule fixed (mitigates DNS response drops).
- 2026-02-02 18:30 UTC: Replace NAT instance with updated CA bundle in AZ-c (mitigates S3/TLS egress failures).
- 2026-02-05 11:45 UTC: Work ongoing to stabilize resolver forwarding across TGW/peering; partial fix applied to route tables in AZ-a to prefer peering.

HYPOTHESES (ordered by likelihood)
1) Asymmetric routing between TGW and VPC peering causes some resolver traffic to take a path that hits a subnet with restrictive NACLs or NAT instance with stale CA. This explains DNS timeouts and TLS unknown CA depending on path.
2) Intermittent certificate errors caused by mixed egress proxies/NAT instances that perform TLS interception or have different trust stores. Some NAT instances lacked Redwood Internal CA chain which caused 'unknown CA' in openssl.
3) Load-balancer or autoscaling group has mixed AMIs: some frontends with correct cert chain, others misconfigured (less likely given cert content inspected on multiple hosts).

OPEN ACTIONS / NEXT STEPS
- [x] Fix NACL ephemeral egress rule in affected AZ (done).
- [x] Replace NAT instance with updated CA bundle in AZ-c (done).
- [ ] Audit all NAT instances across customer VPC for consistent CA bundles and SSM patch status. Owner: Noah. ETA: 2026-02-14.
- [ ] Normalize resolver path: prefer VPC peering path for redwood.internal subnets, avoid TGW for conditional forwards. Owner: Leah. ETA: 2026-02-12.
- [ ] Add monitoring and synthetic checks: from each AZ run dig +short control-plane.redwood.local repeatedly and capture latency/failure rate. Owner: Riley. ETA: 2026-02-11.
- [ ] Add route sanity check to onboarding playbook: verify route tables, peering, TGW attachments, and NACL ephemeral egress rules. Owner: Platform-Engineering. ETA: 2026-02-20.
- [ ] Create KB entry summarizing common private-deploy networking pitfalls (NAT CA drift, NACL ephemeral egress, TGW/peering asymmetry). Owner: Riley/Leah. ETA: 2026-02-18.

NOTES / THINGS TO REMEMBER
- Conditional DNS forwarding + mixed TGW/peering setups are fragile; prefer single consistent path for internal resolvers.
- NACLs are stateless; remember to allow ephemeral port ranges for UDP (DNS) and TCP.
- Keep CA bundles consistent on all egress NAT/proxy instances; include Redwood Internal CA where needed. Automate via SSM document that validates CA presence.
- When debugging intermittent TLS errors, correlate the path (AZ, IP) with which NAT/proxy/NACL was used.

SNIPPETS FOR KB / runbook
- Quick check if DNS failing from host:
  $ dig +short @<local-resolver> control-plane.redwood.local || echo "resolver timeout"
  $ traceroute -n <resolver-ip>
  $ ip route show | grep <resolver-ip>
- Check NAT instance CA bundle quickly:
  $ ssh nat-user@<nat-ip> sudo openssl x509 -noout -text -in /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt | head -n 5
- Check NACL egress ephemeral rule:
  aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc> --query 'NetworkAcls[*].Entries' --output json | jq '.[] | select(.Egress==true)'

END - this is a working scratchpad. Will move to Confluence KB after cleaning.
